questions.question: Describe how to build a stem-and-leaf display for the marks 12, 17, 19, 22, 23, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31, 31, 31, 33, 35, 36, 38, 40, 44, 45, 48.
questions.expected_answer: Stems 1 to 4 in a column with a vertical line. Stem 1 carries leaves 2 7 9; stem 2 carries 2 3 7 8 9; stem 3 carries 0 1 1 1 3 5 6 8; stem 4 carries 0 4 5 8. Count twenty leaves and write the key: 2 | 3 means 23.

questions.question: Why must the frequencies in a table add up to the number of observations?
questions.expected_answer: Each observation receives exactly one tally mark, so the marks and therefore the frequencies count every observation once. A sum that differs from the total shows that something was counted twice or missed, and the rows must be re-tallied.

questions.question: What is gained and what is lost when data is grouped into class intervals?
questions.expected_answer: Grouping shows the shape of the distribution clearly with a few rows, which suits large data sets. It loses the individual values: the table records that eight marks fell between 30 and 39 but not which marks, so the ordered raw data should be kept.
